findings.title: Pre-upgrade daemon without /health pid read dead
findings.problem: answersOnOwnPort requires body.pid === pid, but only the new proxy reports pid in /health. A live daemon started before this change that fails the one-sided start check (forward wall-clock step > 60 s) is read as gone.
findings.impact: checkStatus/stopDaemon clear its state without signalling it and ensureOtlpProxy/spawnDaemon start a second daemon while the old one still holds the port, leaving an orphan. Reachability unconfirmed: it needs an upgrade-time daemon plus a forward clock step.
findings.recommendation: Accept a /health body with no pid as a match on port alone (body.pid === undefined || body.pid === pid), or treat a live pid with a failed start check and a pid-less /health as alive; add a test for a pre-upgrade body.

findings.title: Health timeout clears a live daemon's state
findings.problem: checkStatus and stopDaemon delete the state file whenever isDaemonAlive is false. That includes a live pid that failed the start check and whose /health only timed out (1.5 s shallow deadline) or answered non-ok while busy or restarting. No 'unknown' outcome keeps the state.
findings.impact: A temporary slowdown orphans a running daemon: stopDaemon sends no signal, the next spawn collides on the port. Reachability unconfirmed: it requires a failed start check first.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish 'gone' from 'unknown': when the pid is alive but the start check failed and /health errored or timed out, keep the state (checkStatus) and still signal or refuse (stopDaemon) instead of clearing state without signalling.

findings.title: No-SSO records never count as delivered
findings.problem: When there are no SSO cookies, sendSessionEndMetric returns without setting endMetricSentAt or endMetricSkipped. renameToCompleted is now gated on isDeliveryDone, so for a non-SSO provider (e.g. litellm; the daemon builds the runtime for any provider in claude-desktop mode) the record is never done.
findings.impact: Every daemon start spends an attempt, and after 3 the record is renamed with droppedAt and reported as 'dropped' in analytics, even though no send was ever possible. Reachability unconfirmed: whether claude-desktop telemetry runs with non-SSO providers in practice was not established.
findings.recommendation: When the provider has no SSO credentials by design (non-SSO provider), set endMetricSkipped so isDeliveryDone holds and the record is renamed without a droppedAt mark; keep the retry only for an SSO provider whose credentials are temporarily missing.

findings.title: Daemon stop spends delivery attempts
findings.problem: stop() neither awaits nor cancels startupPass/redeliveryPass, then finalizes each tracked session one after another (lock wait, flush, sync, end metric with a 10 s timeout and retries). stopDaemon sends SIGKILL after 5 s. deliverLocked saves deliveryAttempts+1 before any send.
findings.impact: A stop that is killed partway leaves attempts counted for sends that never completed, and an in-flight pass may hold the lock the stop-time finalize waits on. Together with the 3-attempt cap (CR-004), this pushes records toward being dropped unsent.
findings.recommendation: In stop(), await Promise.allSettled([this.startupPass, this.redeliveryPass]) before finalizing, and bound stop-time finalization (or skip counting the attempt) so a SIGKILL after 5 s does not consume one of the three delivery attempts for a send that never completed.

findings.title: Transcript switch keeps old sync index
findings.problem: On a folder switch, retrackSession points correlation.agentSessionFile at the new transcript but keeps sync.conversations.lastSyncedHistoryIndex and the tracked fingerprint from the old file. Analytics (recordTranscriptPath, cost enricher) also resolve only the new transcript. The test covers only a copy with the same message count.
findings.impact: If the new folder's transcript is not a full copy of the old one, conversation messages are skipped or sent twice, and tokens recorded only in the old transcript are left out of pricing. Reachability unconfirmed: depends on how Desktop writes the switched transcript.
findings.recommendation: When agentSessionFile changes, reset or re-derive sync.conversations.lastSyncedHistoryIndex and the transcript fingerprint against the new file unless it is verified to be a superset copy; cover a new transcript with a different message count in a test, and confirm analytics pricing covers pre-switch tokens.

findings.title: Folder switch may never re-attribute session
findings.problem: EPMCDME-16248 'attributed to the folder where the work happened' is only partly met. retrackSession re-detects branch, repository and project only when discovered.workingDirectory changes. The unchanged discovery (claude-desktop.discovery.ts:202-209) builds that value from companion/metadata originCwd first, and the ticket names originCwd as folder A, which stays the same after the switch. The unit test sets the discovered workingDirectory by hand.
findings.impact: In the ticket's scenario the folder-switch branch may never fire, so the session stays attributed to folder A while the work happens in folder B. Reachability unconfirmed: whether Desktop updates originCwd on a switch was not established, so graded major.
findings.recommendation: Trigger re-attribution from a signal that actually changes on a Desktop folder switch (e.g. the transcript's directory/cwd or userSelectedFolders), not discovered.workingDirectory built from originCwd first; add a test that goes through claude-desktop.discovery with a switched-folder fixture.
